properties.natural_language: A boxed value received for EIP-712 encoding MUST contain exactly three properties: value, primaryType, and types.
The primaryType field in a boxed value MUST reference a type defined within the inner types schema.
The types schema in a boxed value MUST conform to valid EIP-712 type definitions.
After box structure validation succeeds, encodeType MUST produce the format 'box ' || name for boxed members.
After computing hashStruct for a boxed value, the result MUST equal keccak256(innerTypeHash || encodeData(innerValue)).
After type hash computation, the hash MUST be deterministic: the same type string always produces the same keccak256 hash.
Inner type definitions in a boxed value MUST NOT reference any types from the outer struct's type schema (type isolation).
Nested boxes (boxes containing boxes) MUST NOT be supported; inner types cannot use the box keyword.
The EIP-712 domain separator MUST provide replay protection for signed messages containing boxed values.
Before signing, the wallet MUST validate that inner type definitions follow EIP-712 rules and reject invalid schemas.
After successful validation, the wallet MUST render the decoded boxed contents to the user, not opaque hex data.
If type isolation is violated, the wallet MUST reject the signing request.
After ECRECOVER, the recovered signer address MUST match an authorized signer for the operation.
Security considerations for box types MUST include protection against type confusion between outer and inner schemas.
Type schemas in boxed values are immutable once used for signing; versioning is handled at the application level.
After get_blob_parameters returns for an epoch >= 419072, max_blobs_per_block MUST be 21.
After get_blob_parameters returns for an epoch in [412672, 419072), max_blobs_per_block MUST be 15.
Before accepting a block, len(blob_kzg_commitments) MUST be <= the epoch-specific max_blobs_per_block.
If blob commitment count exceeds the epoch-specific limit, the block MUST be rejected.
The proposer_lookahead vector MUST always cover exactly (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) epochs of slot assignments.
All nodes MUST have identical BLOB_SCHEDULE configuration to ensure consistent fork digest computation.
After fork digest computation, the digest MUST incorporate both fork version and blob parameters via XOR.
After proposer lookahead update, get_beacon_proposer_index MUST return in O(1) via state.proposer_lookahead[slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH].
For epochs before the first BLOB_SCHEDULE entry, the system MUST fall back to MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA.
Blob schedule epoch thresholds MUST be set far enough in advance for all nodes to upgrade before activation.
A wallet_sendCalls request from a DApp MUST include a valid version string, chainId in hex with 0x prefix and no leading zeros, and a non-empty calls array.
The app-provided ID in wallet_sendCalls MUST be a unique string up to 4096 bytes for this sender per application.
A wallet_getCapabilities request MUST come from an authorized application for the requested address.
When an untrusted caller queries wallet capabilities, the wallet MUST filter out capabilities that could enable wallet fingerprinting.
After all validation passes and user approval, the wallet MUST generate an unpredictable (cryptographically random) unique batch identifier.
After successful batch execution, all calls confirmed onchain without reverts MUST result in status 200.
If all calls revert, the batch status MUST be 500 (complete chain failure).
If some calls succeed and some fail, the batch status MUST be 600 (partial chain failure).
Batch status transitions are one-way: once a batch moves from status 100 (pending) to any terminal status (200/400/500/600), it MUST NOT revert to pending.
When atomicRequired=true and atomic execution is unsupported, the wallet MUST reject with error 5760 rather than silently execute non-atomically.
The wallet MUST verify that all non-optional capabilities requested in wallet_sendCalls are supported before proceeding.
wallet_getCallsStatus MUST return error 5730 (unknown bundle id) when queried for an ID created by a different application.
Wallet MUST enforce call ordering as specified in the request; calls MUST NOT be reordered.
Chain ID in wallet_sendCalls MUST be a hex string with 0x prefix and no leading zeros.
If a from address is provided, it MUST match an enabled (connected) account in the wallet.
The total number of calls MUST NOT exceed the wallet's bundle size limit.
A speed-up transaction MUST use the same nonce, recipient, value, and data as the original, with at least 10% higher gas price.
A cancellation transaction MUST be a self-send (from == to) with value = 0 and empty data, using the same nonce as the original.
A replacement transaction submitted to the provider MUST have a nonce matching an existing pending transaction.
After a replacement transaction is submitted, the provider MUST emit the appropriate event (tx_speedup, tx_cancel, or tx_replacement) with oldTx, newTx, nonce, and from fields.
After classification, a transaction where only gas changed MUST emit tx_speedup, a self-send with zero value MUST emit tx_cancel, and other field changes MUST emit tx_replacement.
Only the transaction sender can replace their own pending transaction; third parties MUST NOT be able to replace others' transactions.
The replacement transaction MUST be submitted before the original is mined; if the original is already included, the replacement fails.
Each replacement event MUST reference the immediately preceding transaction, not the original, when multiple sequential replacements occur.
The wallet/provider MUST correctly track pending transactions and their nonces to avoid missed or false replacement events.
Input to the MODEXP precompile MUST be parsed as three big-endian uint256 length fields (base_length, exp_length, modulus_length) from the first 96 bytes.
When input data is shorter than declared lengths, missing bytes MUST be zero-padded consistent with EVM memory semantics.
When modulus equals zero, the MODEXP precompile MUST return modulus_length bytes of zeros.
After successful modular exponentiation, the result MUST be left-padded to exactly modulus_length bytes in big-endian format.
Gas cost MUST be at least 200 (minimum floor), calculated as max(200, complexity * iterations / GQUADDIVISOR).
Gas MUST be charged before computation begins; if gas is insufficient, execution MUST halt with OutOfGas.
The gas cost formula complexity = ((max(base_length, modulus_length) + 7) // 8) ^ 2 MUST accurately reflect computational effort.
For exponents > 32 bytes, the iteration count MUST add 8 * (exp_length - 32) to account for additional computation.
When both base_length and modulus_length are zero, the precompile MUST return an empty byte string.
The exponent_head MUST be constructed by taking min(32, exp_length) bytes from the exponent data, left-padded with zeros to 32 bytes.
When exponent is zero and modulus is non-zero, the result MUST be 1 mod modulus.
When base is zero and exponent > 0 with non-zero modulus, the result MUST be 0.
A pull request modifying an EIP MUST include a scope indicator ([Mm]ajor:, [Mm]inor:, or [Pp]atch:) in its commit message.
If no scope indicator is found in the commit message, the PR merge MUST be blocked.
When an EIP transitions from Draft to post-draft status, the version MUST become exactly 1.0.0.
When multiple scope indicators exist in commits, the most severe scope (major > minor > patch) MUST determine the version increment.
After version increment, a changelog entry MUST be generated with version, date, PR number, and description.
PATCH version increments MUST only apply to cosmetic changes (formatting, typos, grammar) that do not alter the technical specification.
EIP authors MUST understand and correctly apply semantic versioning; incorrect increments could cause implementations to misinterpret compatibility.
Fork activation is monotonic: once a fork activates (block_number >= threshold or timestamp >= threshold), it MUST remain active for all subsequent blocks.
Fork ordering MUST place BLOCK_NUMBER forks before TIMESTAMP forks before UNSCHEDULED forks.
An Unscheduled fork's check() MUST always return False (Literal[False]), ensuring it never activates on mainnet.
All nodes in the network MUST agree on fork activation thresholds to avoid chain splits.
Block timestamps MUST be reasonably accurate and not arbitrarily manipulated by validators.
After evaluating fork criteria for a block, exactly one fork's rules MUST be selected for validation.
A block that fails validation under its applicable fork rules MUST be rejected.
All five Constantinople EIPs (145, 1014, 1052, 1234, 1283) MUST activate atomically at the same block; no intermediate states are permitted.
The fork block for each network is fixed: Mainnet=7,280,000, Ropsten=4,230,000, Kovan=9,200,000, Rinkeby=3,660,663. All clients MUST use these exact values.
After the fork block is processed, the chain MUST irreversibly operate under Constantinople rules.
Node operators MUST upgrade their software before the fork block is reached to avoid forking onto a minority chain.
A block received from a peer MUST be validated against the correct ruleset (Byzantium or Constantinople) based on its block number.
The EVM execution loop MUST terminate when evm.running is False OR evm.pc >= len(evm.code).
On ExceptionalHalt, all remaining gas MUST be consumed (evm.gas_left = 0) and output MUST be cleared.
On Revert, remaining gas MUST be preserved (not consumed) and state MUST be rolled back.
Message call depth MUST NOT exceed STACK_DEPTH_LIMIT (1024); exceeding it raises StackDepthLimitError.
Before deploying a new contract, the target address MUST NOT already have code or a non-zero nonce (address collision check).
After contract creation, the deployed code MUST NOT start with the 0xEF prefix (reserved for EOF).
Deployed contract code MUST NOT exceed MAX_CODE_SIZE (24576 bytes).
Gas refund MUST be capped at min(accumulated_refund, gas_used / 5).
Transient storage MUST be properly isolated per transaction and cleared between transactions.
The evm_trace function MUST have no side effects on execution state; tracing cannot alter EVM behavior.
An invalid opcode byte (not in the Ops enum) MUST raise ValueError and halt execution.
After error handling (both ExceptionalHalt and Revert), rollback_transaction MUST be called to undo state changes.
Contract creation gas MUST include len(contract_code) * GAS_CODE_DEPOSIT charged after code validation.
